Why does cutting an onion make you cry?
Why does cutting an onion make you cry?
A whole onion doesn't.
Only a cut one.
Inside each cell,
the onion keeps two
things apart:
a harmless sulfur
compound,
and an enzyme.
Your knife breaks the
cells,
and the two mix.
A second enzyme turns
the result into a
stinging gas.
It drifts up and reaches
the nerves on the
surface of your eye.
Your eye does the only
thing it can:
it makes tears to wash it away.
Chill the onion first,
and the enzymes work
more slowly.
Scientists have even
made onions with almost
none of that second
enzyme.
They hardly make you cry.
The onion isn't sad.
It's a chemical trap,
and your knife springs it.
